collated_index compute a collated index from the site indices, using a Generalized Linear Model.

Source: R/rbms_index_modelling.r
collated_index.Rd

collated_index compute a collated index from the site indices, using a Generalized Linear Model.

Usage

collated_index(
  data,
  s_sp,
  sindex_value = "SINDEX",
  bootID = NULL,
  boot_ind = NULL,
  glm_weights = TRUE,
  rm_zero = TRUE,
  GlmFit = c("glm", "newton", "ipf"),
  SplitGroup = TRUE,
  site_length = NULL,
  index_sites = c("all", "observed")
)

Arguments

data

data.table or data.frame Site indices per year and proportion of flight curve covered by the monitoring.

s_sp

string Species name to be found in the data.

sindex_value

string Name of the response variable to be used the computation of the collated index, default is "SINDEX", but could be other standardized values.

bootID

integer Identify the n^th bootstrap.

boot_ind

data.table Index of the bootstrap and the site ids of the specific bootstrap sample.

glm_weights

logical Use the proportion of the flight curve sampled as weight for the collated index, if FALSE the function uses equal weights.

rm_zero

logical Remove the sites where species was not observed to speed-up the fit of the GLM without altering the output, default TRUE.

GlmFit

character Fitting of the GLM, 'glm' (default, glm()), 'newton' or 'ipf', see details.

SplitGroup

logical When the years form groups not linked through sites with observations, fit each group separately (default TRUE, the correct method). FALSE fits all years together as in previous versions (glm only), the levels of the groups are then arbitrary; 'newton' and 'ipf' always fit the groups separately.

site_length

string Name of a column of data with the length of each site (transect) in km, constant within site, default NULL. With a length, the collated index is the expected count on 1 km of transect (the site effects are divided by the length of the site), otherwise the expected count per site.

index_sites

character Sites the collated index is averaged over: "all" (default) all sites monitored for the species, the sites where it was never observed counting as zero (mean over the monitored area), or "observed" only the sites where the species was observed at least once (mean over the occupied sites).

Value

a list with the collated indices per year (col_index), the site ids of the sample (site_id) and, with GlmFit = 'newton', the year effects (year_effect, see details), NULL otherwise.

Details

Site-years with NA or infinite sindex_value (e.g. years where the flight curve failed) are treated as missing and removed with a warning, as done by site_index; a site with NA in all years is therefore not part of the sample. When boot_ind was generated for a species with boot_sample(s_sp = ), s_sp must be the same species. A bootstrap sample that failed in boot_sample() (NA row) returns NA for the collated index and the number of sites. With GlmFit = 'newton' or 'ipf', the same weighted Poisson GLM (site and year effects) is fitted without building the model matrix (see impute_count for the two methods), which is much faster with many sites and gives the same collated index as glm(). With 'newton', year_effect gives per year the log year effect relative to the first year of each group of linked years (LOG_EFFECT), i.e. the log of the collated index relative to that year, with its quasi-Poisson standard error (SE), an alternative to the bootstrap that ignores the variation among sites. The column GROUP gives the group of years linked through sites with observations in the original data (see n_components), NA for years without observation. When the years form more than one group, the collated index is only comparable between years of the same group (warning): with SplitGroup = TRUE, each group is fitted separately on its own years and sites, its index being the mean over the sites with data in the years of the group, so each group is a separate series. Fitting all years together (SplitGroup = FALSE, previous versions) gives arbitrary levels between groups and can distort the trend within a group, because zero counts of sites observed only in another group enter the fit. The data cannot relate the levels of separate groups. Comparing them rests on the sites of each group being representative of the same population. This holds by design when sites are assigned to years at random, e.g. a rotating panel where a random set of sites is surveyed each year and each site is revisited every few years (each panel then forms a group), but not when the groups result from site turnover, a change in the scheme or different regions. In that case, the groups are separate series. For randomised designs, collated_index_mixed links the groups through a random site effect. The level of the collated index depends on the sites it is averaged over (index_sites) and on the length of the transects (site_length), its changes between years do not. When the level is used as a density, e.g. to weight schemes by their population in a multi-scheme index, see the section "Collated index as a density" of vignette("vignette", package = "rbms").
